answer: Registering a voting agent should consume a nonrefundable 20-token fee. The registry kernel verifies a finalized burn receipt naming the account key and epoch, then marks its transaction ID used. An agent surveying a knoll or inspecting a jetty gets no vote with an invalid or reused receipt. Every extra eligible identity must burn another 20 tokens; parallel registrations cannot share the payment. This assumes valuable scarce tokens, correct receipt accounting and a fee high enough to outweigh the benefit of extra identities.
